query: For an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating susceptible to progressive plastic deformation during continuous loading, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its creep resistance? Specify the governing factor and rationale, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, the operating boundaries under sustained stress, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Coherent BCC nanoprecipitates formed in the FCC high-entropy alloy matrix act as strong obstacles to dislocation motion during sustained loading, thereby reducing the steady-state creep rate via an Orowan looping mechanism.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy coating with negligible secondary phase precipitates
generation.intervention: Thermal aging at 600 °C for 10 h to induce coherent BCC nanoprecipitation within the FCC matrix
generation.conditions: Creep tests at 600 °C under a constant uniaxial stress of 200 MPa for up to 100 h
generation.structural_mediator: Volume fraction (~5–10 %) and average diameter (~20–50 nm) of coherent BCC nanoprecipitates
generation.mechanism: Under load, dislocations bow and loop around coherent precipitates (Orowan strengthening), increasing the stress required for steady-state creep and slowing dislocation climb
generation.predicted_outcome: Aged coating exhibits at least a 50 % reduction in steady-state creep rate compared with the as-deposited baseline
generation.baseline: As-deposited coating steady-state creep rate ~1×10⁻⁶ s⁻¹ at 600 °C, 200 MPa
generation.boundary: Effectiveness maintained between 550 °C–650 °C and 150–250 MPa; above 700 °C or below 150 MPa precipitate coarsening or thermally activated diffusion reduces obstacle strength
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; predicted reduction in creep rate ±20 % due to variability in precipitate size distribution

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two coating specimens (as-deposited and aged at 600 °C/10 h), measure precipitate morphology by TEM, then perform creep tests at 600 °C/200 MPa
measurements: Precipitate volume fraction and size distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if the aged coating either fails to develop coherent BCC nanoprecipitates (volume fraction <3 %) or does not exhibit at least a 10 % reduction in steady-state creep rate relative to the as-deposited baseline.
